description: Node CPU microbenchmark comparing the former full-buffer frontend recomputation on every streaming chunk with the incremental X-ASR frontend. This isolates feature extraction; it is not an end-to-end transcription RTFx claim.

runtime.hardware: local Windows workstation; CPU model not captured

method.baseline: append each chunk to a growing Float32Array and run frontend.process() over the complete accumulated audio
method.candidate: append each chunk to the same growing audio buffer (matching the executor's current metadata cost), then run frontend.processIncremental() over only newly stable frames with a bounded 400-sample tail; flush reflected boundary frames once with final=true
method.correctness: candidate features are compared with one full-buffer process() result; max absolute error must be < 1e-6

caveats: The executor still retains a cumulative audio Float32Array for stream metadata, so this slice removes O(n^2) frontend FFT work but does not yet eliminate cumulative audio-copy allocation.
End-to-end X-ASR encoder and decoder timing must be remeasured on a real artifact before claiming an RTFx improvement.
Right-edge reflected frames are intentionally delayed until the next chunk or finalization to preserve full-buffer parity.
